prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which designed small molecules, whether bifunctional PROTACs or thalidomide-type molecular glues acting through cereblon, direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to chosen proteins

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B023 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, a single prize part. The achievement is a new chemical modality. A designed small molecule brings a chosen protein to an E3 ligase, so pharmacology that depended on occupancy becomes event-driven degradation, and proteins without a conventional binding pocket become reachable. The mechanism is chemically explicit (ternary-complex cooperativity, linker design, the cereblon degron) and independent groups have reproduced it for two decades. The round-1 exchange showed that all eight of us treat the science as original. The remaining disagreement is about credit and timing, not about whether the discovery is real. Crews and Deshaies supply the PROTAC concept and its first demonstrations. Handa supplies the identification of cereblon, which explains an approved class of drugs and shows that the same ubiquitin-ligase logic covers both strands. That is why I think one citation can be honest: it names the shared principle, induced proximity for degradation, and the three names anchor its two roots.
statement.case_against: No bifunctional degrader is approved, so part of the impact is still forward-looking. Whichever three names are used, a decisive contributor is omitted: Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito or Kim. PROTACs and glues have different histories and a sceptic can call the combined citation artificial. If the committee decides maturity should be measured strictly by approved drugs of the designed modality, B002 is the cleaner and safer choice, with the caveats of the 2010 prize and Kosugi's precursor work.

responses.point: Aqvist keeps Ciulli as third name beside Crews and Deshaies, regards cereblon as target identification within one drug class, and says he would not object strongly to Handa.
responses.response: Having reread the exchange, I accept that Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures are the best physical-organic chemistry in the field, and I count his omission as a real cost. My criterion for the third seat is which contribution cannot be removed without making the citation inaccurate. Without Handa, the molecular-glue strand has no mechanism and the citation has to be narrowed to PROTACs only. Without Ciulli, the PROTAC story is still complete as a concept. Your own statement that you could live with Handa, and the fact that five of us name Handa, suggest this can be settled. If the committee narrowed to PROTACs only, I would reconsider and Ciulli would be the better third name. I do not think that narrowing is needed, because cereblon is the mechanism of an approved drug class and not a footnote.

responses.point: Somfai holds B002 first as overdue, with the cleanest attribution on the list and more than two decades of independent confirmation, and he regards B023 as conceptually fresh but harder to attribute.
responses.response: I agree that B002 is the cleanest on attribution and maturity, and your statement that Kosugi's precursor is something a two-name citation sidesteps is fair. My difference is on the 2010 recognition. That prize honoured the field of palladium cross-coupling for bond construction, and C-N coupling is a major but later chapter of it. B023 has no earlier prize behind it and opens targets that were unreachable. I also note that you list B023 as your first alternative and say the timing could be good in a few years. I would ask you to say what you need to see in order to move, since the attribution problem you describe is a feature of every three-person cut in a field of this breadth and is not unique to B023.

responses.point: Zou holds B002 first because it is the only top candidate for which both the discovery and the credit are settled, while admitting she may underweight the novelty of a new drug modality.
responses.response: Your point that credit is settled for B002 is correct and I give it weight. But settled credit is not a reason for a first place when the other candidate carries the stronger science, and you yourself say B023 is conceptually fresher. On maturity, I would separate the strands: the cereblon half has years of approved use in myeloma, so the question of a drug that has not yet been approved applies only to the bifunctional half. I accept that this does not remove the risk. Where we may differ is on what the risk costs, and if the committee votes B023 I hope you can accept Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and tell us whether you would prefer Ciulli in the third place.

responses.point: Brzezinski moved from B028 first and B023 third to B023 first with the same three names as mine, but he lists the lack of an approved degrader as the main reason he did not rank it first originally.
responses.response: We now hold the same configuration, and I do not want this to be read as a count. What I take from your statement is that you weigh clinical immaturity more than I do. My view is that the mechanism and its independent confirmation are the Nobel-relevant tests, and that thalidomide-class drugs already supply a clinical proof of the glue half. I also withdraw my earlier suggestion that B028 might be a serious second candidate unless a single citation and a settled name set can be shown, and in this exchange nobody has shown them.

uncertainties: Whether the combined PROTAC and glue citation is accurate enough with only three names, or whether Ciulli should replace Handa if the citation is narrowed to PROTACs.
Whether the lack of an approved bifunctional degrader should delay recognition by a year or more.
Whether the Somfai and Zou preference for B002 is a matter of principle or ranking, which I cannot tell from their statements.
My knowledge of individual contributions and priority is from memory and has not been independently verified.
statement.conflict_note: No change. I have no recorded personal or institutional tie to anyone in the shortlist, including Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Buchwald, Hartwig, Hyman, Brangwynne or Rosen. My ribonucleotide reductase and dNTP work is thematically near the PCET strand of B028 and some biochemistry here, which I regard as scientific proximity and not a reason to recuse.
